statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-10911: a use-after-free in libxslt, where result tree fragments cached on the transform context were chained through the xmlDoc prev/next pointers that XPath evaluation can also walk, so a crafted stylesheet using key() across result tree fragments can dereference freed memory and crash the process (https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxslt/-/issues/144, https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2397838). The fix, "Use a dedicated node type to maintain the list of cached RVTs", moves that list into a separate xsltRVTList structure. Alpine backported it to 3.23 as CVE-2025-10911.patch in libxslt 1.1.43-r4, whose secfixes list this CVE (https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/commit/8b367fdee54989e3f08a4ce2153d3ad2d25ce42b). The DHI Alpine 3.23 repository publishes libxslt 1.1.43-r3 and 1.1.43-r4 for x86_64 and aarch64. Checked libxslt.so.1.1.43 and libxslt.a of both builds on both architectures: every 1.1.43-r4 copy contains the error string "xsltRVTListCreate: malloc failed" added by the fix and no longer contains the old "Unexpected RVT flag %p" message it replaces, while every 1.1.43-r3 copy has the old message and not the new one. 1.1.43-r4 is the first fixed build.
